## STEWARD6 · STEWARD6-bound — SERVER_US: which measured wait sets the bound (in-round calls, or the polls after a round died)?

Status: **open** · Assigned to: Architect · Revision: 2

### STEWARD6 implementer · Question

Event: `55df10bd6a04e1c54333ee28cbe31ac7` · 2026-10-18T05:33:32Z

> F3's bound is measured; the measurement gives two readings and I need the one that stands. Instrument: a temporary timed line per op in bin/steward.rs (mint, carve, mint-below, attach, open, read, close, stat, grant; a stat is walk+stat+clunk, 3 calls). steward-latency seed 3, rv64 and rv32, 1 and 2 harts, --keep-failed; logs under .worktrees/STEWARD6/.tmp/STEWARD6/measure/, figures in notes.md there.
> 
> Inside completed rounds the worst single call is walfsd:data mint-below (a lease's /project carved below the home): 1.66 s on rv32 at 1 hart in round 4 beside 3 spinners (rv32 2 harts 1.50 s, rv64 2 harts 1.06 s, 1 hart 0.64 s); the worst op is a home stat at 1.62 s (rv64, 2 harts; 3 calls). Reading (a): 2 x 1.66 = 3.32 -> SERVER_US = 4 s.
> 
> But on rv32 a round's loop died on the shell's 5 s start_agent timeout (2 harts: round 3, B88's; 1 hart: round 4 beside 3 spinners, which earlier runs completed: a new miss of F4's kind, borderline at 5.1 s in B88), and after that, with the spinners (10-minute leases) running unopposed, the probe's home_stat polls for the round marker took 4.2, 4.3, 5.1, 5.7, 6.2, 6.6, 8.1, 10.1 s (1 hart) and 4.5 to 7.7 s (2 harts), growing until the bench killed QEMU at 3 h. Reading (b): that is the case's load too; a 3-call stat of 10.1 s bounds one call at <= 10.1 s -> 2 x 10.15 = 20.3 -> 21 s.
> 
> Under (a), in that state a stat or a mint times out: the probe's poll just polls again (no batch); a start_agent's mint fails the step and answers failed, where today it is slow and the client gave up at 5 s anyway: the rule's intent. I recommend (a), 4 s, with the post-death figures and the rv32 1-hart N = 4 miss stated on the page as a residual (a hart saturated by lease VMs puts a server's call past the bound; the step fails and the caller is told). Say if (b) stands, or if a per-call re-measurement (another ~6 h of the latency slot) is wanted before anything is set.

### Architect · Answer

Event: `7a6778f9e19496b99242c8829b3c9ea3` · 2026-10-18T05:33:58Z

> Architect: (a) stands, SERVER_US = 4 s (2 x 1.66 s, rounded up to a second), no re-measurement. Reasons, for the page: the bound is derived from the box serving its load (completed rounds, every caller alive), not from a wedge: the post-death figures are three spinner VMs running unopposed at one hart after the case's own loop died, a server starved of its share, and a bound that admits a 10 s stat would hold the loop 21 s, longer than the callers' own bounds (the shell's 5 s start_agent, sshd's 30 s login), which inverts the rule's purpose. Under (a) the loop is never held past 4 s, under every caller's bound, so a step that fails under the bound is told to a caller still waiting: the rule's intent, as you read it. State on steward.md 'Residual risks' with the bound: the measurement (walfsd:data mint-below 1.66 s, rv32 one hart, N = 4 beside three spinners; the worst op a 3-call home stat 1.62 s), the arithmetic, and the residual in one sentence: a hart saturated by lease VMs of the sponsor's weight puts a shared server's call past the bound; the step fails and the caller is told; the probe's own poll is no batch and only polls again. The rv32 one-hart N = 4 round dying on the shell's 5 s start_agent bound (5.1 s in B88, borderline) is F4's kind: not yours to move; put it in your report under 'For other packages' with the log path, and I will fold it into STEWARD8's brief (its one-hart rows are now in scope too). Ruling file: .wash/local/wave-2026-10-18-rulings.md 'F3' (appended). Remove the timed lines before the commit, as the brief says.
